tier_reason: The IPDPS 2021 paper is still unreachable (ssslab.cn, IEEE and researchgate egress-blocked), so the snippet-backed B stays. Opened an independent peer-reviewed paper (Cong et al., CB-SpMV, ICS '25, via raw.githubusercontent.com) that times TileSpMV against cuSPARSE v12.4 BSR on A100 and RTX 4090; it does not report a TileSpMV-vs-BSR ratio directly, and its averages suggest TileSpMV does not beat best-block-size cuSPARSE BSR on average, so it is recorded as a caveat and not used to raise the tier.

corrections.caveats: Independent measurement (Cong, Sun, Chen, Xie, Liu, Qian, 'CB-SpMV', ICS '25, Salt Lake City; opened): on 2843 SuiteSparse matrices in FP64, with CUDA 12.4 and driver 550.135, each kernel was run 1000 times. cuSPARSE v12.4 bsrmv used the best block size of 2x2, 4x4, 8x8 or 16x16 per matrix, and TileSpMV used 16x16 tiles. CB-SpMV averaged 2.95x over cuSPARSE-BSR and 3.06x over TileSpMV on the RTX 4090, and 2.99x over cuSPARSE-BSR and 3.95x over TileSpMV on the A100. That suggests TileSpMV was on average no faster, and on the A100 slower, than best-block-size cuSPARSE BSR on current GPUs. The ratio of those averages, about 0.96x on the RTX 4090 and 0.76x on the A100, is derived from page data and is only indicative, since averages of per-matrix speedups do not divide exactly. The original IPDPS 2021 paper body (average speedups, cuSPARSE version, precision) remains unopened.
